name: Monte delle doti (Florentine communal dowry fund)
key_source: Anthony Molho, Marriage Alliance in Late Medieval Florence (Harvard UP, 1994), chs. 2-3 (pp. 27-127), Appendix 1 (pp. 351-360); Julius Kirshner and Anthony Molho, 'The Dowry Fund and the Marriage Market in Early Quattrocento Florence', Journal of Modern History 50 (1978): 403-438, doi:10.1086/241732; Julius Kirshner, Marriage, Dowry, and Citizenship in Late Medieval and Renaissance Italy (Toronto, 2015), ch. 4 (pp. 94-113), Appendix 4 and notes (pp. 230-231, 292-309), doi:10.3138/9781442664517; Alan S. Morrison, Julius Kirshner and Anthony Molho, American Journal of Epidemiology 106 (1977): 487-492, doi:10.1093/oxfordjournals.aje.a112496, and American Journal of Public Health 75 (1985): 528-535, doi:10.2105/AJPH.75.5.528. DOIs as given in the bundle README, not re-resolved in this session. Read in full on the text layer; every figure and quotation entering a cell checked on the page image. ONE WITNESS: all five works are by Kirshner, Molho or their co-authors from the fund's own registers; no cell takes high. SCOPE: the communal dowry fund created by PR 114 of 23 February 1424/5, 1425-1530, girls' and boys' accounts and Innocenti foundlings' accounts included. EXCLUDED: the Monte comune except where it pays or prices the fund's own claims; charitable dowry bequests and confraternity subsidies, including the Borromei bequest administered by the Monte (Molho 108-109); other cities' funds; the special gabella of 16 January 1530/1 (1531 modern style) and everything after it. The period ends while the fund still ran: deposits continued to the late 1540s (Molho 70). MS RULINGS 2026-10-15: MC1 = spreading kept; no split (RB2's change at 18 August 1446 / 21 May 1472 recorded in its note); RB4 locator not widened. Kirshner and Klerman, 'The Seven Percent Fund' (Kirshner 2015, ch. 5) to be read after application as an open recoding pass on RB2, LS1, LS2, PY3.
